Senses.Explanation: Literally, dead (死) speech or saying (語). An early sayings record enumerates it among kinds of speech and classifies 'cultivating and attaining buddha,' 'mind itself is buddha,' and similar formulations as unfinal, unblocking, general, accommodating, ordinary-person 'dead speech.' A transmission biography challenges a teacher who 'has a teaching to give people' as having dead speech and asks, 'can dead speech bring people alive?' Another record criticizes taking the ancient people's 'live functioning' as dead speech and supplying matching-stock phrases. A later record deliberately turns the pair: it answers an accusation of dead speech by saying that one unwilling to die under dead speech seeks life in others' live speech, whereas dying there may be followed by suddenly coming alive. The Zen deviation is this technical appraisal of sayings by their recorded handling in teaching and reception, including the corpus's own reversal; it is not simply a synonym for false words.
Senses.Note: Allowlist count: 99 hits in 42 texts. One speech-category sense. The texts' contrary appraisals do not create separate referents. Family checked against dead phrase (死句), live phrase (活句), live saying (活語), dead teaching (死法), and dead words and dead sayings (死言死語).

Occurrences.Kwic: 雲門氣宇如王。甘死語下乎。澄公有法授人死語也。死語其能活人哉。
